description:
We are three students specializing in E-Health and AI, passionate about technology, healthcare, and space exploration. We aim to develop innovative AI-powered health monitoring software for astronauts.

We’re looking for motivated teammates with skills in Python, AI, machine learning, data science, and web development.

Let’s innovate together and take healthcare beyond Earth!
summary: ASTRA BIOGUARD is an individualized biological digital twin and predictive countermeasure platform designed for long-duration spaceflight. Instead of relying on generic terrestrial population averages, ASTRA BIOGUard evaluates crew health strictly against each astronaut's pre-flight baseline (Day 0) and directional risk tolerances. The platform integrates a 3-step loop (GATHER-EVALUATE-ACT) processing 10 longitudinal biomarkers and transcriptomic data, connects to live NASA OSDR and NCBI research repositories, provides a dual-mode interface (Flight Surgeon telemetry vs. Astronaut daily portal), features a predictive "What-If" intervention simulator, and enforces mandatory human medical sign-off before executing countermeasures.
details:
What exactly does it do? ASTRA BIOGUard tracks and forecasts individual physiological drift for astronauts across 6 mission milestones (Day 0 to Day 180). It flags multi-system anomalies in bone, muscle, and cardiovascular health, models preventative interventions, and coordinates communication between ground control and orbit.

How does it work? It runs on a pure, deterministic TypeScript biological engine (biologicalEngine.ts) that calculates personal percentage deviations (computeDirectionalDeviationPct) against individual baselines rather than static population thresholds. It pairs this with structured Gemini AI clinical synthesis (/api/ai/analyze) and a "What-If" countermeasure trajectory simulator.

What benefits does it have? It eliminates the "population average trap," catching silent bone and muscle loss early, reduces cognitive overload in orbit via a dedicated Astronaut Portal, and ensures strict safety through human-in-the-loop flight surgeon sign-off.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use? • Frontend & Backend: React, TypeScript, Node.js, Express, Tailwind CSS, SVG Charts. • Database & Sync: Firebase Auth & Cloud Firestore (with local localStorage fallback). • APIs & Intelligence: Google GenAI (Gemini), NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR), NCBI E-utilities, and Ensembl REST APIs
dataRefs: NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR / GeneLab) via live proxy requests ([https://osdr.nasa.gov/osdr/data/search
projectRefs: • NCBI E-utilities (GenBank, ClinVar, GEO Datasets for genetic variant and gene expression context). • Ensembl REST API (GRCh38 gene coordinates and variant consequences). • Published spaceflight medical literature (NASA Twins Study, Sibonga et al. on bone resorption, Fitts et al. on skeletal muscle adaptations).
